authorityLimit: Prospective tasks and grading criteria are assessed. No actual learner, laboratory execution or source-research performance occurred. A/D/native/source blockers remain independent and unresolved.

records.reason: The two cases distinguish branched uncrosslinked chains from networks and require a conditional assignment of Y. A 5% residual strain alone does not prove a dense thermoset network. Application choices depend on the stated thermal and load conditions.

End-carbon radicals, chlorine retention and combination conserve atoms. Ethen/styrene versus vinyl chloride plus a scavenger changes substituent and active centres. Conversion falls from 60% to 5%; this does not establish chain length or safety.

Four linear monomers form three links and release three water or HCl molecules, with correct end groups. The explicitly demanded second comparison changes nucleophile and electrophile. Actual acid/amine synthesis conditions are not claimed from a paper mechanism.

40/80=0.50 and 100/75≈1.33 kWh/kg PET are correct. Pyrolysis feedstock is not equivalent PET. The changed mixture gives 28+45=73 kg target products and 27 kg outside those products. Missing cost and impact data limit the choice.

10^6 to 2×10^4 is a 98% reduction/factor 50. 90% to 95% is five percentage points; dissolved Ag 2 to 8 is fourfold. Primary particles, aggregates, abrasion, controls and detection limits are distinguished. Efficacy alone does not prove safety.

Tg concerns amorphous segment mobility, Tm crystalline regions. A covalent network can soften above Tg without melt flow. Cooling history/crystallinity and a load cycle are real variations. Q has melted crystallites at 180°C; 210°C remains unresolved without degradation and viscosity data.

PE and PA6,6 repeat structures are correct. 35%/60% crystallinity and 250/900 MPa require a structure explanation, not only a name. Styrene/divinylbenzene crosslinks require both vinyl groups to connect different chains; the conditional limitation is explicit.

PLA molar mass 100 to 20 under sterile conditions shows chain cleavage; 60% CO2 shows partial mineralisation. Cellulose glycosidic cleavage with 65% versus 5% sugars and no CO2 is distinct from 30% CO2 partial mineralisation. The cases vary chemistry and conditions meaningfully.

The same PE can have different feedstock origins. 20 g bags are compared using CO2e, water and land rather than equating CO2e with energy. The reuse expressions 200/n+c give break-even 20 uses for X and 12 for Y; at five uses 50/42 g remain conditional. Collection is not recovered-product yield.

50 PP boxes use 5 kg/90€ versus 20 kg/100€; ten uses give 10 kg/140€. The composite 3/0.1=30 h break-even and 100 h saving of 7 kg are correct. A pilot 0.8 versus 4 kg is not a whole-system result. The grading asks for explicit conditions and missing information.

A linear PDMS trimer from three bifunctional monomers releases two waters; each Si has four single bonds and each bridging O has two. Oil versus network and a 40 nm film are distinct; film thickness does not establish nanoparticles. Equal chemistry with wetting 105°/35° versus 155°/5° isolates texture, while dirt removal and abrasion remain untested.

Injection moulding, extrusion, calendering and blow moulding are represented correctly. A finished network has no melt flow at 230°C and decomposes at 240°C. Extruding the flowable precursor at 190°C and subsequently crosslinking is a conditional alternative, not remelting the final network.

For cubes, 20 nm versus 2 μm gives 3×10^8 versus 3×10^6 m−1, ratio 100; 30/300 nm spheres give ratio 10. A 155° angle alone does not prove a lotus effect. Immobilised 70%/0.2 mg versus loose 80%/12 mg varies release and efficacy; neither establishes safety.

10−3 to 10^4 S/m is a factor 10^7. sp3 interruption and doping are meaningful changes; contact effects motivate four-point measurements. Equal nominal doping does not prove equal mobile-carrier concentration or mobility.

At equal geometry, 100 Ω/0.1 g polymer versus 0.002 Ω/0.8 g metal supports different sensor/power choices. After wet bending both materials fail; disentangling wetting from bending needs a factorial control. The cases assess criteria and limits rather than material labels.

A lactic-acid trimer releases two waters; the PLA repeat is correct. Lactide ring opening does not release water per ring. Crystalline B at 80°C and amorphous A film composting are conditional observations; A does not prove B composts equally.

Alternating, statistical, block and graft structures are distinguished from blends. Equal 50/50 composition does not fix sequence. K recovery 20% versus 100% and hard-domain loss at 80°C support physical domains, not permanent covalent crosslinks.

O attack on isocyanate C with C=N pair movement to N and proton transfer is a valid formal route; equivalent justified mechanisms are allowed. 200/200 versus 210/210 OH/NCO balances and triol networking are conditional. 2 mmol water produces 2 mmol CO2, consumes 4 mmol NCO and leaves 96 mmol; no actual execution is claimed.

−360 versus −208 kJ/mol gives 152 kJ/mol stabilisation relative to the stated hypothetical comparison. Six p orbitals/six π electrons form the benzene system. An open conjugated diene with four p orbitals/four π electrons is not aromatic; energetic data do not identify a reaction barrier.

Equivalent 139 pm C–C bonds conflict with fixed alternating bond lengths. Contributors do not exchange as molecules in equilibrium. Changing a ring atom to sp3 by addition interrupts delocalisation; substitution with rearomatisation preserves the ring system.

A 470 nm LED emits blue light; a clear material absorbing 450–490 nm may look approximately yellow in white light under the stated simplifications. Red 630 nm is blocked while green 540 nm is transmitted in the second case. No fluorescence is inferred.

An opaque blue reflector with negligible other reflectance can be dark under 590 nm illumination. A 5/5/80% versus 5/40/80% three-band comparison makes B brighter at 550 nm without fixing an exact colour coordinate. The changed source probes actual transfer.

A +M donor and −M nitro acceptor can alter the chromophore. Protonation shifts 510 to 430 nm, raising excitation energy. A bridge giving 500 nm versus interrupted 330 nm moves the supplied dominant band to UV. Other bands and conditions remain relevant; no universal donor rule is asserted.

At the same 500 nm maximum, 0.90 to 0.45 absorbance represents half concentration under the stated Beer–Lambert assumptions, not changed excitation energy. X+Y gives 0.8/0.2/0.7 at the three supplied points; detection at 450/650 nm does not uniquely identify all mixture components.

Both designed cases are chemically assessable: diazotisation conserves N/O/H and charge, followed by azo-coupling sigma complex/deprotonation; the other route uses carbonyl activation, aryl attacks, water loss and leuco oxidation with balanced H+/electrons. Changed protonation and R substituent are substantive. Design Pass cannot clear the independent non_atomic decision.

The cases correctly distinguish wool ammonium/sulfonate attraction and cellulose hydroxyl interactions from covalent fixation. The second case demands triazine-Cl reactive fixation versus neutral polyester dispersion. The graded answer does not use the image’s universal ladder. Case-design Pass coexists with this unresolved native-context block.

I+2e−⇌L2− is a valid alkaline reduced-leuco formal relation. Teacher-prepared reagents and authorised SOP constrain execution. Blank logs and the rubric require real observations for the practical expectation; provided text cannot earn it. The air-time/direct-dye comparison is a controlled prospective variation. This is design review only.

The fictional 200→600 employees, 20→120 t output, price 12→5 and research 4→30 provide assessable relationships. Railway expansion is a confounder. Dye share 70→35 is −35 percentage points; constant total revenue does not establish overall profitability or welfare without costs and other data.

At pKa 7, pH 6/8 gives base/acid ratios 0.1/10. HIn and In− are distinct species, not contributors. B++H++2e−⇌BH balances charge; absorption at 530–700 nm leaves blue 430–480 nm in the simplified model. Reoxidation by air is not proof of a pH change.

Br2/FeBr3 formal electrophile bookkeeping is accepted without asserting freely solvated Br+. NO2+ ring attack shifts an N=O pair to avoid invalid nitrogen valence. Toluene under light gives radical side-chain reaction, distinct from catalysed ring substitution. No exact isomer yield is invented.

The supplied C1+ sextet/C2− lone-pair contributor conserves atoms and net zero charge but has lower weight than neutral contributors. Neutral symmetry-related contributors are equivalent. Moving H produces a changed nuclear arrangement and is not resonance.

Phenol pKa 10 versus ethanol 16 and anilinium 4.6 versus cyclohexylaminium 10.6 are interpreted within the same aqueous comparison. Chloroacetic 2.86 versus chloropropionic 4 and acetic 4.76 probe inductive distance. Nitro substitution lowers aniline N basicity; values are not transferred across solvents without qualification.

The benzene Group 1 statement is treated as hazard identification, not personal probability or a verdict for all aromatic substances. Closed process versus open cleaning changes exposure. Fictional volatile R versus dusty S requires route-specific information; no complete toxicity conclusion follows from volatility alone.

1240/2.48=500 nm and 1240/4.13≈300 nm; 2.0/3.1 eV gives 620/400 nm. Increased gap gives a hypsochromic shift. The cases require the relation and spectral limitations, not an exact colour name inferred from one band.

The tasks require actual source lookup with recorded identity, context and uncertainty; author summaries alone cannot earn research credit. Equal colour/fastness is not equal toxicology. EFSA’s actual food-colour and additive pages were checked for the bounded function/safety-assessment statements. Oral food evaluation does not establish textile/dermal safety.

Neutral toluene/phenol/aniline generally direct ortho/para, nitro meta; activation and direction are different judgments. Anilinium has no available N lone pair and changes directing behaviour. Actual protonation/reaction conditions matter; no pure-isomer quota is assumed.

The attacked C1 has four bonds (H, electrophile and ring neighbours), with positive ring charge represented at C2/C4/C6. Rearomatisation removes H+, not hydride. Nitro N+/O− notation preserves octet; ring +1 and counterion bookkeeping conserve overall charge, with HSO4− giving H2SO4.
